content:
I was {a}born in a Dublin street, where the {G}royal drums do beat,
and the {a}loving English feet, they tramped all {G}over {a}us,
and each {C}day and every night, when my {G}father'd come home tight,
he'd in{a}vite the neighbours {G}outside with his {a}ch{G}or{a}us.

Oh, come {a}out ye Black and Tans, come out and {G}fight me like a man.
Show your {a}wives how you won medals down in {G}Flan{a}ders.
Tell them {C}how the I.R.A. made you {G}run like hell away
from the {a}green and lovely {G}lanes of Kille{a}sha{G}ndr{a}a.

Oh, come tell us how you slew them poor Arabs two by two,
like the Zulus they had spears and bows and arrows.
How you bravely faced each one with your sixteen-pounder guns
and you frightened them poor natives to their marrows.

Oh, come let me hear you tell, how you shamed the brave Parnell,
when you thought him well and truly persecuted.
Where are all the sneers and jeers, that you bravely let us hear,
when our heroes of sixteen were executed.

Oh, the day is coming fast and the time is here at least
when each human will be cast aside before us.
And if there will be a need, sure my kids will sing good speed,
with a verse or two of Steven Behan's chorus.
title: The Black and Tans
info:
Der Song nimmt Bezug auf den Irischen Unabhängigkeitskrieg und die IRA, die gemeinsam mit der republikanischen Partei Sinn Féin eine eigenständige irische Republik ausriefen.

Der Titel bezieht sich auf die Black and Tans, eine britische paramilitärische Gruppierung, die in den 1920er Jahren zur Bekämpfung der IRA von der britischen Regierung gebildet wurde. Ihre Aufgabe war die Unterdrückung und Bekämpfung der republikanischen Freiheitsbewegungen in Irland. Dabei ging sie mit Unterstützung von britischen Polizeikräften äußerst brutal vor.

Behan selber stammt aus einer politisch sehr engagierten Familie, sein Vater war Mitglied der IRA und kämpfte im irischen Befreiungskrieg gegen die britischen Truppen. Auch Dominic Behan war Mitglied in der Jugendorganisation der IRA und veröffentlichte mehrere Gedichte in deren Zeitung.

Weitere Strophen:
Allan, Larkin and O'brien how you breavely called them swine,
Robert Emmet who you hung and drew and quarterd.
High upon that scaffold high, how you murderd Henry Joy
And our Croppy Boys from Wexford you did slaughter.

Oh, come out you british sones, come out and fight without your guns
Show your wives houw you won medals up in Derry!
How you murderd sixteen man and you'll do the same again
So get outa here and take your bloddy army.
